passages.text: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz was the son of Jotham.
Jotham was the son of Uzziah.
Rezin was king of Aram.
Pekah was king of Israel.
Pekah was the son of Remaliah.
Rezin and Pekah marched against Jerusalem.
They came to fight a war against the city.
They could not defeat Jerusalem.
They could not overpower the city.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן־ יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן־ עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן־ רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
He belonged to the house of David.
Someone brought news to the house of David.
The report said, “Aram has joined with Ephraim.”
Ahaz heard this news.
His people also heard it.
Their hearts trembled with fear.
They shook like trees in a forest.
The wind shakes the trees.
In the same way, fear shook Ahaz and his people.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נָ֥חָֽה אֲרָ֖ם עַל־ אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֤נַע לְבָבוֹ֙ וּלְבַ֣ב עַמּ֔וֹ כְּנ֥וֹעַ עֲצֵי־ יַ֖עַר מִפְּנֵי־ רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field, and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Isaiah.
Isaiah was a prophet.
The LORD told Isaiah to go out.
Isaiah was to take his son Shear-jashub with him.
The LORD told Isaiah to meet Ahaz.
Ahaz was the king of Judah.
Isaiah was to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct.
This aqueduct supplied water to the upper pool.
The meeting place was on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
The LORD told Isaiah what to say to Ahaz.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz to be careful.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz to stay calm.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz not to be afraid.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz not to let his heart be weak.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz not to fear the two kings.
These two kings were like two smoldering stubs of firewood.
These kings were Rezin and the king of Aram.
The other king was the son of Remaliah.
These kings were angry.
Isaiah was to tell Ahaz not to fear their anger.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל־ יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ צֵא־ נָא֙ לִקְרַ֣את אָחָ֔ז אַתָּ֕ה וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ אֶל־ קְצֵ֗ה תְּעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־ מְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵ֠לָיו הִשָּׁמֵ֨ר וְהַשְׁקֵ֜ט אַל־ תִּירָ֗א וּלְבָבְךָ֙ אַל־ יֵרַ֔ךְ מִשְּׁנֵ֨י זַנְב֧וֹת הָאוּדִ֛ים הָעֲשֵׁנִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בָּחֳרִי־ אַ֛ף רְצִ֥ין וַאֲרָ֖ם וּבֶן־ רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃

passages.text: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’
passages.sermon:
Aram is a nation.
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
The son of Remaliah is a leader allied with them.
These three have made a plan against Judah.
They have decided to harm Judah.
They say, “Let us go up against Judah.
Let us attack Judah.
Let us break Judah apart for ourselves.
Let us set up a king in Judah.
Let us make the son of Tabeal king there.”
passages.original: יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־ יָעַ֥ץ עָלֶ֛יךָ אֲרָ֖ם רָעָ֑ה אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּבֶן־ רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ נַעֲלֶ֤ה בִֽיהוּדָה֙ וּנְקִיצֶ֔נָּה וְנַבְקִעֶ֖נָּה אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וְנַמְלִ֥יךְ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ אֵ֖ת בֶּן־ טָֽבְאַֽל׃ס

passages.text: But this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘It will not arise; it will not happen.
passages.sermon: The Lord GOD speaks.\r\nHe says, “It will not arise.\r\nIt will not happen.”
passages.original: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה לֹ֥א תָק֖וּם וְלֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.
passages.sermon:
Aram is a nation.
Damascus is the capital city of Aram.
Rezin is the ruler of Damascus.
Ephraim is another nation.
In sixty-five years, Ephraim will be destroyed.
Ephraim will no longer be a people.
passages.original: כִּ֣י רֹ֤אשׁ אֲרָם֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְרֹ֥אשׁ דַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק רְצִ֑ין וּבְע֗וֹד שִׁשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה יֵחַ֥ת אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעָֽם׃

passages.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Samaria is the capital city of Ephraim.
The leader of Samaria is the son of Remaliah.
God speaks to the people.
God says, “If you do not believe, you will not stand.”
God warns that faith is necessary to remain strong.
passages.original: וְרֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וְרֹ֥אשׁ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן בֶּן־ רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ אִ֚ם לֹ֣א תַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּ֖י לֹ֥א תֵאָמֵֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, saying, “Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again.
The LORD said to Ahaz, "Ask for a sign from the LORD your God."
You may ask for a sign from the depths below.
Or you may ask for a sign from the heights above.
passages.original: וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר׃ שְׁאַל־ לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת מֵעִ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ הַעְמֵ֣ק שְׁאָ֔לָה א֖וֹ הַגְבֵּ֥הַּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃

passages.text: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was the king of Judah.
Ahaz spoke to the LORD.
Ahaz said, “I will not ask for a sign.”
Ahaz said, “I will not test the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז לֹא־ אֶשְׁאַ֥ל וְלֹֽא־ אֲנַסֶּ֖ה אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Isaiah spoke to the house of David.
Isaiah said, "Listen now, house of David."
You test the patience of people.
Is this not enough for you?
Will you also test the patience of my God?
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙ הַלְא֣וֹת אֲנָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י תַלְא֖וּ גַּ֥ם אֶת־ אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God.
The Lord will give you a sign.
Look.
A virgin will become pregnant.
She will give birth to a son.
She will call His name Immanuel.
passages.original: לָ֠כֵן יִתֵּ֨ן אֲדֹנָ֥י ה֛וּא לָכֶ֖ם א֑וֹת הִנֵּ֣ה הָעַלְמָ֗ה הָרָה֙ וְיֹלֶ֣דֶת בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥את שְׁמ֖וֹ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.
passages.sermon:
A special child will be born.
This child will be called Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey.
He will eat these foods before He knows to reject evil.
He will eat these foods before He knows to choose good.
passages.original: חֶמְאָ֥ה וּדְבַ֖שׁ יֹאכֵ֑ל לְדַעְתּ֛וֹ מָא֥וֹס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָח֥וֹר בַּטּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to King Ahaz of Judah.
God promised a sign to Ahaz.
A special boy would be born.
This boy would be called Immanuel.
Before this boy could choose good or reject evil,
the land of the two kings Ahaz feared would be destroyed.
God would make these lands empty and wasted.
Ahaz would no longer need to fear these two kings.
passages.original: כִּ֠י בְּטֶ֨רֶם יֵדַ֥ע הַנַּ֛עַר מָאֹ֥ס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָחֹ֣ר בַּטּ֑וֹב תֵּעָזֵ֤ב הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה קָ֔ץ מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י מְלָכֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on the house of your father a time unlike any since the day Ephraim separated from Judah—He will bring the king of Assyria.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD will act.
The LORD will bring trouble upon you.
The LORD will bring trouble upon your people.
The LORD will bring trouble upon your father’s house.
This trouble will be greater than any since Ephraim separated from Judah.
The LORD will bring the king of Assyria.
passages.original: יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־ עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ יָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ בָ֔אוּ לְמִיּ֥וֹם סוּר־ אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֖ת מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃פ

passages.text: On that day the LORD will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has great power over all nations.
On that day, the LORD will act.
The LORD will call the flies from the farthest streams of Egypt.
The LORD will also call the bees from the land of Assyria.
The LORD will summon these creatures by whistling to them.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines and clefts of the rocks, in all the thornbushes and watering holes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD will call foreign armies to invade the land.
These armies will come like swarms of flies and bees.
They will fill every steep ravine.
They will settle in the clefts of the rocks.
They will be in all the thornbushes.
They will be in every watering hole.
passages.original: וּבָ֨אוּ וְנָח֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ בְּנַחֲלֵ֣י הַבַּתּ֔וֹת וּבִנְקִיקֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים וּבְכֹל֙ הַנַּ֣עֲצוּצִ֔ים וּבְכֹ֖ל הַנַּהֲלֹלִֽים׃

passages.text: On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates —the king of Assyria—to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to remove your beard as well.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the subject.
The Lord is powerful and acts with authority.
On that day, the Lord will act.
The Lord will use a razor.
This razor comes from beyond the Euphrates River.
The king of Assyria is the razor.
The Lord will use the king of Assyria as an instrument.
The Lord will shave your head.
The Lord will shave the hair of your legs.
The Lord will also remove your beard.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יְגַלַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָי֩ בְּתַ֨עַר הַשְּׂכִירָ֜ה בְּעֶבְרֵ֤י נָהָר֙ בְּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר אֶת־ הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְשַׂ֣עַר הָרַגְלָ֑יִם וְגַ֥ם אֶת־ הַזָּקָ֖ן תִּסְפֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: On that day a man will raise a young cow and two sheep, and from the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for all who remain in the land will eat curds and honey.
passages.sermon:
On that day, a man will live in the land.
He will keep a young cow.
He will keep two sheep.
The cow and the sheep will give much milk.
The man will eat curds from the milk.
Everyone who remains in the land will eat curds and honey.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא יְחַיֶּה־ אִ֛ישׁ עֶגְלַ֥ת בָּקָ֖ר וּשְׁתֵּי־ צֹֽאן׃ וְהָיָ֗ה מֵרֹ֛ב עֲשׂ֥וֹת חָלָ֖ב יֹאכַ֣ל חֶמְאָ֑ה כִּֽי־ חֶמְאָ֤ה וּדְבַשׁ֙ יֹאכֵ֔ל כָּל־ הַנּוֹתָ֖ר בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And on that day, in every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver, only briers and thorns will be found.
passages.sermon:
On that day, God will act in judgment.
Every place that once had a thousand grapevines will change.
Each vine was worth a thousand pieces of silver.
Now, these places will not have vines.
Briers will cover the land.
Thorns will grow everywhere.
People will not find fruit there.
They will only see briers and thorns.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֣ה כָל־ מָק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִֽהְיֶה־ שָּׁ֛ם אֶ֥לֶף גֶּ֖פֶן בְּאֶ֣לֶף כָּ֑סֶף לַשָּׁמִ֥יר וְלַשַּׁ֖יִת יִֽהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the land will be covered with briers and thorns.
passages.sermon: Men will go to that place.\r\nThey will carry bows and arrows.\r\nBriers and thorns will cover the whole land.
passages.original: בַּחִצִּ֥ים וּבַקֶּ֖שֶׁת יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה כִּי־ שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה כָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: For fear of the briers and thorns, you will no longer traverse the hills once tilled by the hoe; they will become places for oxen to graze and sheep to trample.
passages.sermon:
The hills once tilled by the hoe will change.
People will not go there anymore.
They will fear the briers and thorns.
Oxen will graze on these hills.
Sheep will trample them.
passages.original: וְכֹ֣ל הֶהָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּמַּעְדֵּר֙ יֵעָ֣דֵר֔וּן לֹֽא־ תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְהָיָה֙ לְמִשְׁלַ֣ח שׁ֔וֹר וּלְמִרְמַ֖ס שֶֽׂה׃פ
